answer.summary: Answered inside the repository, not by outside research. The nationwide-government lane found the dating evidence already present in the locked artifacts: each Nebraska section prints its own amendment history and Minnesota's page prints its general-revision date. Those provisions were added to the compiler's temporal-review map — the same mechanism Missouri, Nevada, Ohio, New Jersey and Massachusetts already used — and each review names the exact bytes on the locked page that date the words, so the compiler refuses to promote unless it finds them. Minnesota reads its revision date verbatim: 1974-11-05, one label for the whole restructured constitution. Nebraska's labels give a year rather than a day, so validFrom is the January 1 after ratification, a bound the page proves rather than a precise effective day it does not state: art. III sections 1 and 12 and art. IV section 1 from 2001-01-01, art. III section 7 from 1989-01-01, art. III section 8 from 1995-01-01, art. IV section 2 from 1967-01-01. Verified independently here by reading the generated corpus at that commit: all 69 rows are now EXACT_INTERVAL and none is CURRENT_OBSERVATION. Both states open on an ordinary start, and a life reaching a seat before those words took effect is still told the rule is unknown.

question: For each of ten named provisions of the Minnesota and Nebraska constitutions, on what date did the provision's current words take effect, and what primary or publisher material establishes that date?

title: When the present words of ten Minnesota and Nebraska constitutional provisions took effect
usableAnswer: A row per provision: the citation, the date the current language took effect, whether that is a ratification date or a later stated effective date, and the material that establishes it — a ratification note, an election canvass, a session-law or amendment record, or the constitution's own provision on when an amendment takes effect. Where a provision has been amended since and the current words are older or newer than the article's headline date, say which. If a provision's commencement genuinely cannot be established from available material, say that with what you checked; an honest unknown keeps the present refusal, which is the safe outcome, and is far better than a guessed date.
whyItMatters: Nobody can stand for office in Nebraska, and the Minnesota House refuses the same character the Senate accepts. The cause is not a rule and not a bug: the game will not apply a constitutional requirement to a date earlier than the day it observed the text, and the ordinary start date is January 5, 2026 while these texts were read on September 9, 2026. That discipline is right and has already caught real provenance leaks, so the repair is not to relax it. The repair is the commencement date, which is the fact the EXACT_INTERVAL rows already carry and these ten do not. With it, two states become playable without anything being assumed.
